chunks: And ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAlī al-Ḥalabī narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

"The salat of advancing combat is on the back with gesturing by your head and takbir. In close sword-fighting, it is takbir without gesturing. In pursuit, it is gesturing; each man prays according to his own situation."

key_terms.إِيمَاءٌ: performing prayer motions by gesture rather than full physical movement
key_terms.بِرَأْسِكَ: with the head, indicating head gestures for prayer
key_terms.تَكْبِيرٌ: uttering 'Allāhu Akbar' as part of the prayer
key_terms.حِيَالِهِ: according to his own condition or immediate circumstance
key_terms.صَلَاةُ: the ritual prayer being discussed in a legal context
key_terms.ٱلزَّحْفِ: advancing combat or military movement toward the enemy
key_terms.ٱلْمُسَايَفَةِ: close fighting with swords or direct armed engagement
key_terms.ٱلْمُطَارَدَةِ: pursuit or chasing in combat circumstances

ai.seo_question: How is salat performed during battle, close combat, and pursuit in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives rulings for salat in conditions of intense fighting and movement. It explains how the prayer is adjusted according to the level of combat, preserving the obligation of worship even in hardship and danger.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1346 - Ubaydullah ibn Ali Al-Halabi reported from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) who said:

"The prayer during advancing combat (al-zahf) is performed on one's back with gestures of the head and the takbir (proclamation of 'Allahu Akbar'). During close fighting (al-musayafa), it involves takbir without gestures. During pursuit (al-mutarada), it is performed with gestures, and each person prays individually as per their situation."
